tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: 1st Disclosure on September 27, 2023 The Company had informed stock exchanges regarding receipt of a Show Cause Notice (SCN) on September 27, 2023 from Directorate General of GST Intelligence, Pune Zonal Unit under Section 73(1) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 (“the Act”), alleging a tax demand of ₹17,28,86,10,803/- on grounds of non-payment of GST on the Co-insurance premium accepted as follower in case of co-insurance transactions and non-payment of GST on re-insurance commission accepted on the reinsurance premium ceded to various Indian and Foreign reinsurance companies during the period July 2017 to March 2022. The SCN referred to matters which are relating to industry wide issues. 2nd Disclosure on December 28, 2023 The Company had informed stock exchanges vide intimation dated December 28, 2023 regarding receipt of an order on December 27,2023 with respect to aforesaid SCN confirming GST demand of ₹17,288,610,803/- and levying a penalty of ₹1,728,861,079/-. Subsequently, the Company had filed a writ petition before the Hon’ble Bombay High Court against the said Order. 3rd Disclosure on July 03,2025 The Company had informed stock exchanges vide intimation dated July 03, 2025 that the Company has received a communication from its tax advisors on July 2, 2025 regarding the order passed by the Hon’ble Bombay High Court (Hon’ble Court) setting aside the order passed by the adjudicating authority confirming the said demand. The Hon’ble Court has noted that the GST Council has considered the issue and also issued Circulars in this regard. The Hon’ble Court has therefore directed the adjudicating authority to re-hear the matter in light of the decision of the GST Council and the Circulars. 4th Disclosure on September 30,2025 The Company has informed stock exchanges vide intimation dated September 30, 2025 regarding receipt of an order from Additional Commissioner, CGST & Central Excise Palghar Commissionerate on September 29, 2025 confirming GST demand of ₹ 17,288,610,803/-, levying a penalty of ₹ 1,728,861,079/- and Interest u/s 50 of CGST Act, 2017 for the period July 2017 to March 2022. The Order refers to matters which are relating to industry wide issues. The Hon’ble Court noted that the GST Council had considered the issue and also issued Circulars in this regard. The Hon’ble Court had therefore directed the adjudicating authority to re-hear the matter in light of the decision of the GST Council and the Circulars. The matter was re-heard by the GST authorities on receipt of directions from Hon’ble Bombay High Court vide order dated 30 June 2025. Despite, the circulars issued, the Company has received an order confirming the demand. Based on the advice of its tax advisors, the Company would pursue an appeal with Appellate Authorities/ evaluate any other appropriate actions against the said Order including filing of writ petition.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Additional Commissioner of CGST & Central Excise, Palghar Commissionerate
tax_litigation.status: The Company has filed writ petition before Hon’ble Bombay High Court against the said Order on December 23,2025.

operating_notes.text: FY26 gross written premium was ₹30,618.09 Cr, of which ₹1,835.46 Cr was written outside India.
Investments were ₹58,421.27 Cr at March 31, 2026, with investment income of ₹4,730.86 Cr.
The company has no subsidiaries, associates or joint ventures in India or outside India.
Motor book split is 50-50 between own damage and third party, versus an industry skew of 40% OD and 60% TP.
Retail health grew 69.5% in Q1FY27 with market share up to 4.5% from 3.5%; long-term book was 53.4% of new retail health business.
IL TakeCare app GWP was ₹154.5 Cr in Q1FY27 versus ₹93.2 Cr a year ago, with 22.1 million downloads.
Q2FY27 net retention ratio rose to 80.67% from 75.27% a year ago, lifting net premium growth to 17.0% against 9.1% gross premium growth.
Health group/corporate underwriting loss was ₹301 Cr in Q2FY27 versus ₹97 Cr a year ago; motor underwriting loss narrowed to ₹33 Cr from ₹72 Cr.
Fire segment posted a ₹68 Cr underwriting profit in Q2FY27 versus ₹104 Cr a year ago.
Q2FY27 motor underwriting loss narrowed to ₹33 Cr from ₹72 Cr a year ago; fire posted a ₹68 Cr underwriting profit versus ₹104 Cr.
Health group/corporate underwriting loss was ₹301 Cr in Q2FY27 versus ₹97 Cr a year ago.
The company booked ₹169.40 Cr of motor TP claim reserves for the Supreme Court's June 11, 2026 homemaker ruling, of which ₹165 Cr was in Q1FY27.

timeline.summary: ICICI Lombard reported FY26 PAT of ₹2,772 Cr (+10.5% YoY) with a combined ratio of 103.4% and proposed a final dividend of ₹7 per share.
ICICI Lombard received a revised GST appellate order for ₹3.06 Cr penalty and ₹0.72 Cr interest for April 2018 to May 2019.
ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Limited, led by **Vikas Mehra**, scheduled analyst/institutional investor meets on June 2, 4, 8, and 23, 2026, in Mumbai via in-person conferences.

ICICI Lombard filed its FY26 Integrated Annual Report and 26th AGM notice (meeting June 19, 2026), seeking shareholder approval for ₹12,772 Cr of FY2028 related-party limits with ICICI Bank and ICICI Securities Primary Dealership; auditors gave an unmodified opinion.
Q2FY27 results (standalone): revenue ₹6,651.87 Cr, net profit ₹946.4 Cr (+15.5% YoY).
ICICI Lombard hosted an earnings conference call on October 14, 2026, discussing Q2 and H1 2026-27 performance with **Vikas Mehra**, CFO.
ICICI Lombard hosted Q2 FY2027 earnings call reporting PAT of ₹1,031 Cr up 27.5% YoY.
ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Limited scheduled an in-person investor meet with analysts/funds on October 23, 2026, in Mumbai via Vikas Mehra.
ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Limited scheduled five investor/analyst meets in Mumbai, November 3–17, 2026, with Bernstein, Ashika, Avendus, CITIC CLSA, and JM Financial.
